page: Amazon Web Services t3.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture burstable instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 2.5 GHz, configured with 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the t3.xlarge delivers modest performance, generally placing in the bottom 25% or bottom 10% across multiple standardized tests. The stress-ng single-core CPU score is 1140.79, and the multi-core score is 3253.57. Memory bandwidth tests show 167.53 GB/sec for cached small blocks and approximately 23.93 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In application-specific tests, the instance achieved 2.65 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 2.74 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Due to its burstable CPU allocation model, the t3.xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads with variable or intermittent CPU utilization. However, the tradeoff is limited sustained compute capacity, as sustained high CPU usage will deplete CPU credits and restrict performance to baseline levels. This resource profile is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as development environments, low-traffic web servers, small databases, and microservices that experience periodic traffic spikes rather than continuous high-intensity processing.
